text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated cluster ded-3b reporting sustained elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts for tenant Pegasus. 5xx rate 12% over 5m, gateways returning 502/504. Paging Sam (oncall). link: https://redwood.inc/alerts/2315120000

Sam (oncall): I’m on it — pulling traces and logs now. ETA 5.

Elaine (sre): vitals from ded-3b: GPU utilization 94%, KV mem pressure high, eviction rate spiked. Could be noisy tenant or cache thrash.

Devin (runtime): seeing a lot of upstream 504s from model-worker pods for pegasus routes. Prefetch failures and large seq lengths from some requests.

Maria (customer-ops): Customer reported major API errors ~5m ago, they’re seeing 502s in production and are starting to page their SREs.

Sam (oncall): quick impact check: which routes are affected and approximate p50/p95 latency?

Devin (runtime): affected route: /v1/generate (model: rwd-open-13b) for the Pegasus tenant. p50 ~800ms -> p50 ~1.6s, p95 spiking to 12s and 5xxs.

Kai (infra): I’m checking pool capacity. ded-3b has 3 spare nodes but autoscale not triggering due to quota on this tenant pool. Looks like tenant pegged KV cache and causing eviction storms.

Sam (oncall): Can we isolate tenant traffic to spare pool or force fallback to a lower memory model? We need to stop the immediate customer errors.

Devin (runtime): Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) Reroute Pegasus to spare-pool (non-disruptive) 2) Apply per-tenant concurrency throttle 3) Enable model variant rwd-open-7b fallback for new requests.

Elaine (sre): Agreed. I’ll coordinate the reroute and keep a rollback path.

Kai (infra): Preparing reroute command. Executing:
```
# reroute tenant Pegasus to spare pool
redwoodctl route set --tenant pegasus --target pool:ded-spare-1 --drain 60s
```

Ops-Bot: Command accepted. Started draining pegasus connections on ded-3b. Estimated cutover 45s.

Sam (oncall): Applying a soft throttle on /v1/generate to 30rps for Pegasus to limit burst while we monitor.

Devin (runtime): Applied throttle. Also toggled fallback:
```
# enable fallback to 7B model for latency-sensitive paths
redwoodctl config set --tenant pegasus --route /v1/generate --fallback rwd-open-7b
```

Ops-Bot: Fallback config updated.

Maria (customer-ops): I’ve notified Pegasus support lead: "We’re actively rerouting your traffic and enabling a fallback to a smaller model to reduce errors; this should reduce 5xx within a minute. Monitoring closely."

(45s later)
Sam (oncall): cutover finished. Telemetry: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 3% in next 2m. p95 down to ~1.8s. Good first signal.

Elaine (sre): KV eviction rate trending down. ded-3b mem pressure reducing. But there are residual timeouts from in-flight requests — still seeing occasional 504s.

Devin (runtime): I pulled one worker log for a failing request:
```
[2026-03-15T12:08:34Z] ERROR worker: request processing timeout after 12000ms, seq_len=4096, kv_cache_miss=high
Trace: model-run -> kernel-alloc failed: out-of-memory (alloc 512MB)
```

Kai (infra): That log matches a pattern where large sequence-length bursts plus caching pressure cause kernel alloc failures on GPU. We'll need a longer-term guard (per-request max-seqlen and tenant burst protection).

Sam (oncall): For now we should keep throttle and fallback in place until Pegasus confirms stabilization. Any need to escalate to oncall-manager?

Maria (customer-ops): Pegasus confirms traffic is back to their baseline; they see occasional degraded responses but errors dropped drastically. They asked for an RCA and ETA for permanent fixes.

Elaine (sre): I’ll keep this incident open for handoff to engineering for root cause. Sam, can you prepare notes for the postmortem? Include commands and timeline.

Sam (oncall): On it. Quick timeline (first pass):
- 2315120000 Alert: ded-3b elevated 5xx
- 2315120025 Paging Sam
- 2315120050 Identified tenant Pegasus heavy r/w and KV thrash
- 2315120105 Reroute to ded-spare-1 initiated
- 2315120148 Throttle + fallback enabled
- 2315120215 5xx reduced to ~3%

Devin (runtime): Will open a runtime ticket: enforce per-tenant request size limits, backpressure when KV eviction > threshold, and automatic fallback when worker OOM patterns are detected.

Kai (infra): I’ll open infra ticket: enable autoscale override for tenant pools when sustained GPU util >90% and eviction rate high; add spare buffer to dedicated pools.

Elaine (sre): Immediate post-incident actions:
- Keep throttles and fallback until 24h of stable telemetry
- Notify billing/ops about any customer impact credits (TBD)
- Schedule postmortem in 48h with runtime+infra+customer-ops

Sam (oncall): Closing the live paging. Marking incident as mitigated. If anything regresses, re-open this thread.

Ops-Bot: Incident state -> MITIGATED by Sam (oncall) at 2315125400.

Maria (customer-ops): I’ll own comms + coordinate postmortem invite with Pegasus.

Elaine (sre): Notes for postmortem doc: attach logs from ded-3b, routing change diff, throttle/fallback config, and the exact reroute command output.

Devin (runtime): Ticket created: RUNTIME-4829 "Per-tenant seqlen & OOM backpressure"
Kai (infra): Ticket created: INFRA-3311 "Autoscale override + spare buffer for dedicated pools"

Sam (oncall): Thanks team. Incident mitigated, follow-ups assigned. :thumbsup:
